title: Targeted repro scaffold and focused regression tests for incident-driven eval gaps
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Context: A recent production incident showed a sudden quality regression tied to a model/serving-config mutation. Existing eval pipelines capture aggregate metric deltas but lack a fast way to: (1) materialize a compact repro dataset tied to the change, (2) auto-generate focused smoke tests that reproduce the observed behavior, and (3) attach config/model delta metadata to the new tests so future rollouts block on regressions.

Objective: Build a lightweight incident-driven repro scaffold that can be invoked from postmortems or CI when an eval gap is detected. The scaffold should produce a prioritized set of hypothesis-driven examples, instrumented with request context (model version, quantization/profile, sequence length, runtime kernel selection, routing path). It should also provide an automated path to convert those examples into durable regression tests that run in the eval smoke suite and link back to the config delta that produced them.

Scope: This ticket covers design and an initial implementation for host+dedicated deployment incidents. Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) will be tracked but handled in a follow-up (separate ticket). The output will include: repro harness code, a PR template that auto-populates test metadata, pipeline changes to record delta IDs, and a dashboard panel showing repro coverage vs. recent regressions.

Why this is different: Unlike broad synthetic eval generation, this work focuses on producing minimal, high-signal repro cases tied directly to the production payloads and decision path. The goal is to reduce debug time and prevent repeated regressions by making postmortem artifacts actionable and testable.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible repro harness exists (python CLI + internal library) that can take an incident id or config-delta-id and output a focused repro corpus (<=500 examples)
Each repro example includes metadata: model_version, config_delta_id, seq_len, tokenization fingerprint, routing path, kernel hints
An automated conversion from repro corpus -> regression test entry is implemented and submit-able as a GitHub PR using an internal template
CI runs the generated tests in the smoke eval suite and blocks merges if new test fails on baseline model
Dashboard tile added showing: active repro artifacts, linked config deltas, and pass/fail trend for auto-generated tests
Documentation (Confluence) with runbook for on-call to generate repros and create tests is published
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Initial triage summary: incident tied to config-delta 'cfg-2026-03-08-41' showed 8-point drop on MSR-clarity eval. Spike recommended: capture top 200 failing requests and attempt minimal input trimming to isolate failure region.

2026-03-11 - Diego Martinez: Implemented a spike that pulls failing requests and runs a tokenizer-fingerprint pass. Found that 62% of failures have an unusual long-prefix tokenization split linked to 'kv-ttl' default. Pushed proof-of-concept code to internal repo: github.com/redwood-inference/repro-harness/pull/18

2026-03-12 - Product review (Lara Singh): Agree on scope. Request we include a small UX for engineers to mark examples as 'signal' vs 'noise' to speed triage. Also asked to add a label for customer-impacting repros.

2026-03-12 - Diego Martinez: Added interactive selection UI to the CLI (flag --interactive) and added metadata field 'customer_visible' in generated test template. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/repro-harness/pull/22

2026-03-13 - Reliability (Marco Alvarez): Noted dependency on eval infra retention window; we need a short-term workaround for archived requests older than 7 days. Created ticket ENG-96501 to extend short-term retention for incident repros.

2026-03-14 - Ava Chen: Merged initial harness into staging and ran end-to-end: incident -> repro corpus -> auto-PR -> CI smoke run. Two follow-ups: (1) add kernel-selection metadata extraction in runtime agents (ENG-96730), (2) hook into rollout pipeline to mark config deltas as 'blocked-by-failing-auto-tests'
notes: Trade-offs discussed: We intentionally limit the repro corpus size to <=500 examples to keep CI cost and noise low. If the incident suggests broader distributional drift, the scaffold will flag and create a separate 'broad-eval' ticket rather than auto-generating a large test suite.
Edge cases: For private deployments we will surface the harness but not auto-submit PRs; teams can export the repro corpus as a tarball and run locally under their controls.
Future: Tie the repro harness to the eval-alerting pipeline so that significant deltas can optionally kick off an auto-repro job overnight and email a summary to the incident owners.
